claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT at 0 K can identify a ferromagnetic ground state by comparing the total energies of different magnetic configurations.
CoCrFeMnNi is an example of a 3d transition-metal alloy to which the proposed method can be applied.
The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is nominally chemically disordered and crystalline.
Distinct ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and nonmagnetic initializations can be evaluated using spin-polarized DFT.
The proposed calculations represent energy-minimized states at 0 K under periodic boundary conditions using a plane-wave basis.
The relevant structural mediator is the local alignment of spins associated with partially filled 3d orbitals on the transition-metal sublattice.
Spin-polarized DFT captures spin-dependent exchange and correlation effects.
Parallel alignment of magnetic moments can lower the total energy relative to nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic configurations.
For the proposed alloy, the ferromagnetic configuration is predicted to have a lower total energy than the nonmagnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations.
The predicted lowest-energy configuration has a nonzero net magnetization consistent with ferromagnetism.
A non-spin-polarized DFT treatment would omit the energy gain associated with spin alignment and predict no magnetization.
Thermal fluctuations at nonzero temperature may reduce or eliminate ferromagnetic order.
The predicted magnetic moment can vary with exchange-correlation functional, lattice parameter, and chemical composition.
Static 0 K DFT calculations do not fully capture finite-temperature magnetic effects.
Low-temperature SQUID or VSM measurements can test the predicted net magnetization.
